test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 09 Feb, 2026 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
In the given figure, PQ is parallel to BC . Angle CPQ = 45 degrees and angle APQ = 75 degrees. What is the value (in degrees) of angle CPB ?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2dce483251c580580ac6b7f7856d2c1ed6e375cc0608030f61ff10e90c156b86.png]
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since PQ || BC, the corresponding angle ∠ABC = ∠APQ = 75°.

Also, the alternate interior angle ∠PCB = ∠CPQ = 45°.

In triangle PBC, the sum of all internal angles is 180°.

∠CPB = 180° − (∠ABC + ∠PCB) = 180° − (75° + 45°) = 60°.

**∴ The correct answer is 60°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** PQ || BC, ∠CPQ = 45°, ∠APQ = 75°.

**Formula Used:** Linear pair axiom (Angles on a straight line sum to 180°).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/17075def9a2ad9cdd9bf1ac3194b75e1d314c51475861d019d136e48fc8d23ed.png] 

⇒ In the figure, A, P, and B are points on a straight line segment AB.

⇒ The sum of angles at point P along the line AB is 180°.

⇒ ∠APC = ∠APQ + ∠CPQ

⇒ ∠APC = 75° + 45° = 120°

⇒ ∠APC + ∠CPB = 180° (Linear pair)

⇒ 120° + ∠CPB = 180°

⇒ ∠CPB = 180° − 120°

⇒ ∠CPB = 60°

**∴ The correct answer is 60°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Corresponding Angles

When two parallel lines are intersected by a transversal, the angles in matching corners are equal (∠APQ = ∠ABC).

Alternate Interior Angles

When parallel lines are cut by a transversal, the angles on opposite sides of the transversal and inside the parallel lines are equal (∠CPQ = ∠PCB).

Linear Pair Property

Angles that lie on a straight line always sum up to exactly 180°.
